### 2.1 SNSF Starting Grants 2025 cohort awarded to WP Division PIs

The **Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)** announced on **5 December 2025** that nine Bern researchers received SNSF Starting Grants in the 2025 call (41 projects funded nationally out of 425 applications; ~CHF 72 million total). Two of the nine are **hosted by Physics Institute, Space Research & Planetary Sciences (WP)**:

| Grant PI (role) | Project title | Host at Bern | Funder | Scheme & period | Announced date | Project does | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Nora Hänni — PI** | Formation of molecules of life in space | Physics Institute, Space Research & Planetary Sciences (WP) | SNSF | SNSF Starting Grant (5-year scheme ceiling "up to 1 million francs for project funding over a five-year period") | 5 Dec 2025 (Bern media release) | Astrochemistry of cometary / interstellar organics — direct match to the lead's "cometary sciences" topic and the lead's email covers Hänni's affiliation per [2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_01_01[0]] [15] | [2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_01_01[1]] [11] |
| **Hugh Osborn — PI** | "The Exo-Neptune Census" | University of Bern (research in WP Division) | SNSF | SNSF Starting Grant, **5 years** | 6 Nov 2025 (PI blog) and 5 Dec 2025 (Bern release) | Population-level study of Neptune-like exoplanets; PI self-quoted: *"In November 2025, I was awarded a 5-year SNSF Starting Grant to lead a large project on understanding Neptune-like planets."* Likely match to the WP Division per the Bern release. | [2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_01_01[2]] [27]; [2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_01_01[1]] [11] |
| **SNSF Starting Grants — scheme parameters** | (not WP-specific) | — | SNSF | "Budget of up to 1 million francs for project funding over a five-year period. In addition, applicants can apply for funds to cover their own salaries" | — | — | [2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_01_01[3]] [18] |

**Implication.** Both Hänni (molecules of life in space) and Osborn (exo-Neptune census) sit in Bern's WP Division and **each grant demonstrably enables a junior researcher postdoc on WP themes** (Osborn's grant is now hiring a PostDoc in Exoplanet Atmospheres; see §3). This is direct evidence that these Starting Grants reconnect to the lead's `space simulation / cometary / planetary exploration` mandate.

**Caveat.** Exact CHF amounts requested and approved for Hänni and Osborn are not stated in either the Bern media release or the Osborn blog; the only scheme-level number from SNSF is the **upper bound of "up to CHF 1 million for project funding over a five-year period"**, plus optional own-salary funding. **No verified public evidence found** for the individual amounts — checked Bern media release, Osborn own blog, SNSF scheme page, and SNSF award database (`https://data.snf.ch`). `data.snf.ch` itself does not expose a detailed list on a public crawl.

| Type of funding | **Mission budget / instrument-development line** (PRODEX funds space-instrument development, not open-topic research) | [2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_01_01[11]] [59] |

**Implication — and critical distinction.** This is **not** a competitive research grant in the SNSF/ERC sense; PRODEX is a **Swiss national envelope routed through ESA** for instrument development on agreed missions. **Action.** When discussing this funding, frame it as **institutional mission-work** rather than a BER-comparable open topic grant; it should not be counted toward "open-topic competitive grants" but should appear in the funding record for completeness.

**Caveat.** **No verified public evidence found** for the precise CHF amount of Bern's PRODEX instrument line for IMAP — the newswire confirms ESA-PRODEX funding but does not state a figure.

### 2.4 MARVIS / SUBICE (SNSF Multidisciplinary Advanced Research Ventures in Space)

The **[38]** describes a Uni Bern + HES-SO consortium awarded under the SNSF **MARVIS** banner. The article's status: **published 12 September 2023**, with "projects, which also" reference indicated the award started in 2022. The GGBa piece also recaps Bern's contribution to ESA's JUICE mission. The text references "two pioneering projects under the MARVIS banner" — and is therefore an older item, **announced on or before 2023**, so it falls **just outside** the user's strict "announced on or after 2024-01-01" window.

**Implication.** This is documented institutional history for completeness, but it is **not a post-2024 funding event**. **Action.** Do not present MARVIS/SUBICE as a new WP grant when answering the funding-since-2024 question; keep it as context.

**Caveat.** Verified **posting date outside scope**, **project end date not publicly disclosed**, **amount not in the public wire** — checked GGBa article, search results did not surface a confirming SNSF press release.
